title: Export generated skinned creatures to a standard glTF/GLB artifact
description:
## Summary
Add an editor export path for the generated creature's actual animation-ready representation so a creature can be shared outside Unity and uploaded for inspection. Prefer glTF 2.0 / GLB because it is a standard portable 3D interchange format with native skeleton/skin/bone-weight support and can be inspected without a CreatureCreator-specific importer.

## User Mandate
"A way to export the mesh, especially with all of the animation weights and whatnot, would be ideal. Especially if it can be a fairly simple standard exportable format such that I can share it with you."

## Scope
- Export the generated implicit skinned surface with vertices, normals, indices, submeshes, materials/vertex colors where representable, skin joints and weights, bind poses, and the resolved semantic skeleton.
- Export rigid mesh-asset geometry as mesh primitives using their existing rigid binding information, once those items are installed/represented through the same rig mapping.
- Preserve mirror identity and bone ordering exactly as the runtime binding uses them.
- Emit a self-contained `.glb` when practical; a `.gltf` + binary buffer fallback is acceptable only if it materially simplifies the implementation.
- Keep exporter/editor concerns out of runtime generation and animation hot paths.
- Make export deterministic for identical generated creature input.
- Include stable semantic bone IDs/names in node extras or equivalent metadata so an exported artifact can be traced back to CreatureCreator's skeleton.

## Performance
Export is an explicit user action. It may be comparatively expensive, but must not alter generation or per-frame animation performance. Do not add export-specific work to `CreatureRig.ApplyPose`, `SkinnedMeshRenderer` binding, or the procedural generation hot path.

## Validation
- Export a representative `dinus_uprightus` creature.
- Validate the resulting artifact with a standard glTF validator or importer when available.
- Confirm vertex counts, triangle counts, bone count, weights, and bindposes match the Unity representation.
- Open/import the exported artifact and confirm rest-pose and a known test pose are spatially consistent.
- Confirm no source/generated mesh is mutated during export.
- Add focused editor tests for deterministic output and weight/bone count parity.

## Ownership
Parent under the animation/presentation workstream. This is an editor/export feature, not a runtime animation dependency.

## Non-goals
Do not build a new animation system, locomotion system, general asset pipeline, or custom proprietary mesh format. Do not make Unity package/runtime code depend on the exporter.

## Status
Backlog.

## Rationale
A standard glTF artifact provides a much better diagnostic boundary than screenshots alone: it makes the actual mesh, skeleton, bindposes, and weights independently inspectable while remaining substantially simpler and more portable than an FBX-specific pipeline.
